questions.title: Which candidate will receive the most “encourage” votes in the first UN Security Council straw poll of the 2026 secretary-general selection?
questions.background: António Guterres is serving as UN secretary-general. Informal Security Council straw polls gauge support for potential successors, with members indicating whether they encourage, discourage or have no opinion on each candidate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official UN information or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations describing the first Security Council straw poll in the 2026 secretary-general selection process. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the candidate receiving the highest number of “encourage” votes in that first poll, regardless of subsequent polls or the final appointment. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-23 AFP / France24 reporting ahead of tonight's televised General Assembly debate (2100 GMT, broadcast by Bloomberg) confirms the exact 6-candidate field and locks in the first closed-door UNSC straw poll for July 30 (one week away). International Crisis Group UN expert Richard Gowan told AFP today: 'I find that Grossi is still the mostly frequently mentioned front-runner, but he has not locked the race up. Other candidates like Grynspan and Rodrigues-Birkett also have significant numbers of admirers.' AFP similarly singles out IAEA chief Rafael Grossi as the most repeatedly mentioned contender, nudging Grossi ahead into #1 (0.39 -> 0.43) and trimming Rebeca Grynspan slightly (0.40 -> 0.36) in a still-tight two-way lead. Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett (2024-25 UNSC colleague, GRULAC woman without P5 baggage) jumps from #5 to #3 (0.03 -> 0.08) on Gowan's explicit endorsement of her broad Council appeal in an approval-style first poll. Macky Sall trims 0.09 -> 0.07 (only non-GRULAC nominee, carrying domestic repression criticism despite Senegal's endorsement), and Michelle Bachelet trims 0.06 -> 0.04 (alienated both China over Uyghur report and the US, plus Chile withdrew backing), leaving 2% residual for 6th nominee Maria Fernanda Espinosa.

questions.title: Which European country will announce plans to shut down its only nuclear power plant because of drought-related cooling-water shortages by August 2, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear power plants that use river water for cooling can face operational restrictions when drought reduces the available water supply.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Rule : Identify the European country whose government announces, between July 1 and August 2, 2026, inclusive, plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant because drought has reduced the river water available for reactor cooling. The announcement of the shutdown plan is sufficient; the shutdown itself need not have occurred. A partial reduction in electricity output alone does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.

(2) Hungary climbs 0.20 -> 0.26 (new #2): BME nuclear engineering dean Attila Aszodi warned on ATV.hu (July 21) that the Danube at Paks fell 6 cm below its all-time record low (-104 cm Friday, -71 cm Tuesday), all three cooling parameters (temperature, level, flow) hit critical marks simultaneously, Paks was 'only a few cm' from a turbine shutdown and 25-30 cm from a complete plant shutdown, and 'we are not past the hardest part' (moderated slightly vs. Romania because Paks has 4 units with staged shutdown buffering). (3) Slovenia drops 0.36 -> 0.21 (#3): no mid/late-July Krsko cooling alerts, Krsko's auxiliary cooling towers held 100% power through June's heatwave, and Reuters (July 21) reported storms spreading directly into Slovenia—though single-reactor exposure keeps it a serious #3. Bulgaria (Kozloduy, 0.14 -> 0.13) faces the same record-low Danube (lowest since 1946 in Serbia) without reported cooling alerts yet; Belarus trims 0.02 -> 0.01 (sum 0.99).

questions.title: Which club will sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: Bruno Guimaraes joined Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022 and has established himself as a prominent Premier League midfielder.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Newcastle United or the receiving club confirming a completed permanent transfer during the 2026 summer transfer window. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the receiving club in the first completed permanent transfer of Guimaraes from Newcastle United during that window. Loan moves, reported interest and unconfirmed agreements do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the receiving football club.
questions.current_reasoning: Major Tier-1 confirmation across July 21-24 (The Times, BBC Sport's Sami Mokbel on July 23, Fabrizio Romano & ESPN on July 24): Arsenal have opened formal club-to-club talks with Newcastle United that have 'accelerated in recent days,' fully agreed personal terms with Bruno Guimaraes ('the contract is ready'), and are preparing an official £70m bid after a £55m+£10m package was discussed/rejected, with Guimaraes informing Newcastle internally of his preference to join Arsenal and Mikel Arteta pushing hard (to the point Arsenal starter Martin Zubimendi is exploring talks with Real Madrid/Barcelona). Promoting Arsenal 0.55 -> 0.63 (strictly capped below 0.65 pending fee agreement/official announcement because BBC and Romano note Arsenal have a hardline valuation cap and previously walked away from Morgan Rogers when Chelsea bid £117m); keeping Manchester City at 0.10 (above Real Madrid 0.11 -> 0.08) as the prime hijack threat if Rodri leaves for Madrid, trimming Barcelona 0.06 -> 0.04 after signing Gordon, PSG 0.05, and 10% residual.

questions.title: If the Detroit Tigers trade Tarik Skubal by the 2026 MLB trade deadline, which team will acquire him?
questions.background: Tarik Skubal is a starting pitcher for the Detroit Tigers and is eligible for free agency after the 2026 season.

Passan (July 21, giving Skubal 60% overall trade odds) named six realistic best fits: Dodgers, Braves (0.17), Cubs (0.14), Rays (0.12, also cited by USA Today's Bob Nightengale alongside Houston), Phillies (enters at 0.07, replacing the New York Yankees who were omitted from all July 21-22 suitor lists), and Brewers.
